userStories.title: Dispatch RULE as a reviewer AGENT job
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add RULE to FlowStep together with its exhaustive dispatch case and typed task input.

**Motivation** — The flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, Steps, step 2.5) says the finish is "Arc A's rulings by agent, then the ready step"; Arc A (#390) already lets an agent rule an item and a `FIX` apply the rulings.

**Approach** — `FlowStep` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-steps.ts:3`). Baseline: `'SPEC_REVIEW' | 'PLAN' | 'PRD_REVIEW' | 'RUN' | 'REVIEW' | 'FIX'`. Target: adds `'RULE'`.

`buildStepDispatch` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-step-dispatch.ts:30`) and `BuildStepDispatchInput` (:14). Target: input gains optional `rule?: { ref: string; prNumber: number; items: FlowOpenItem[]; guidance: FlowRuleGuidance | null }`; a `RULE` case returns `{ command: 'AGENT', feature, ref: rule.ref, bashMode: 'raw', agent: { name: reviewAgent, task: buildRuleTask(...), model: flow.reviewerRole } }` plus the common fields.

`FlowStep` gains `RULE` together with the `RULE` case of the exhaustive `buildStepDispatch` switch, so the type check stays green. RULE is read-only; the existing AGENT dispatch path is reused, not a new command or permission. Missing rule input throws `RULE requires the RUN branch and PR`. Preserve all existing step bodies and their assertions in flow-step-dispatch.spec.ts.

**Scope** — In: RULE type, dispatch input/body, common remaining-cap/repo/pinned-runner propagation and seam to US-001 buildRuleTask. Out: when to choose RULE (US-007/008), loading RUN/guidance (US-011), ruling persistence (US-005/010). A flow-side code fix that does not go through `FIX` (`nax bot fix`); RULE never pushes.

**Interface**
```ts
rule?: { ref: string; prNumber: number; items: FlowOpenItem[]; guidance: FlowRuleGuidance | null };
```

userStories.title: Support SYSTEM-authored Arc A rulings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend ruling attribution, FIX snapshot naming, system comments and the API ruling contract to SYSTEM.

**Motivation** — Arc A (#390) already lets an agent rule an item and a `FIX` apply the rulings.

**Approach** — **Ruling actor.** A flow ruling is stored with `actorType: 'SYSTEM'`, `actorId: 'flow'` (the column is a string, no migration) and the flow's `approvalRequestId`; it runs under `runAsSystem('flow', ..., { onBehalfOf: creator })`, as the flow's stop tickets do. The Finish ticket is created with the creator's principal; the ruling comment is a system-authored `RULING` comment. `snapshotForFix` sends it to nax as `by: koda:system:flow`. The actual createForFlow writer and action context belong to US-005; this story supplies the actor representations and comment primitive.

`FleetPrRuling.actorType` (`apps/api/src/fleet/rulings/fleet-pr-ruling.domain.ts:15`). Baseline: `'USER' | 'AGENT'`. Target: `'USER' | 'AGENT' | 'SYSTEM'`. `FleetPrRulingDto.actorType` (`apps/api/src/fleet/rulings/dto/fleet-pr-ruling.dto.ts:14`) enum: `['USER', 'AGENT', 'SYSTEM']`.

`pendingForFix` (`apps/api/src/fleet/rulings/prisma-fleet-pr-ruling.repository.ts:98`). Target: a `SYSTEM` row's `actorName` is its `actorId`, with no user or agent lookup.

`snapshotForFix` (`apps/api/src/fleet/rulings/fleet-pr-rulings.service.ts:33`). Baseline `by` is `koda:agent:<name>` or `koda:user:<name>`. Target: a `SYSTEM` ruling is `koda:system:<actorId>`.

`FleetJobTicketEffects` (`apps/api/src/fleet/tickets/fleet-job-ticket.effects.ts`). Target: adds `createSystemRulingComment(ticketId: string, body: string): Promise<{ id: string }>` over the repository's existing `createSystemComment(ticketId, body, CommentType.RULING)`.

**The ruling contract.** `FleetPrRulingDto.actorType`'s enum gains `SYSTEM` and `openapi.json` is regenerated (`bun run api:export-spec`) in the same story, as F4b did for its route; the web and CLI types are out of scope. The generated spec diff is only this enum change. Add repository and DTO unit specs, the koda:system:flow case next to existing USER/AGENT snapshot cases, and the ticket-effects case; existing assertions are unchanged.

**Scope** — In: actor union/Swagger metadata, repository naming, snapshot attribution with existing non-fatal head-read failures preserved, system RULING comment primitive and root OpenAPI artifact. Out: principal loading and system write context (US-005), flow-feature migration (US-006), advance integration (US-010/011). `SYSTEM` in the web (`apps/web/lib/fleet-types.ts`) and generated CLI ruling types; the API DTO and `openapi.json` are updated.

**Interface**
```ts
actorType: 'USER' | 'AGENT' | 'SYSTEM';
createSystemRulingComment(ticketId: string, body: string): Promise<{ id: string }>;
```

userStories.title: Require human guidance for each held FIX round
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make the FIX decision wait for fresh human guidance in NAX flows while preserving completion and stop semantics.

**Motivation** — Live flows 7-9 (fleet design doc §9.174-§9.176) reach `FIX`, but a draft PR whose open items need rulings stops the flow `pr_not_ready`, and the human has to rule each item through `POST .../fleet/jobs/:id/rulings` and dispatch `FIX` by hand.

**Approach** — `decideFlowStep` PR-phase rules (single-feature flows; all earlier rules unchanged):
6. `FIX` COMPLETED and ready (`markedReady` true, or false with no `readyHeld`) -> `complete` (unchanged).
7. `FIX` held, `readyHeld` starting with `CI ` -> stop `pr_not_ready` with `readyHeld` (unchanged detail).
8. `FIX` held, `canApplyCalls` false, or `fixReady` null -> stop `pr_not_ready` (unchanged).
9. `FIX` held (nax entry): `questionsJobId === job.id && answers !== null` -> `dispatch RULE` with `rule: { answeredJobId: job.id }`; otherwise `wait_answer` step `FIX`, one question id `1`: `PR still held after FIX <id>: <readyHeld>. Answer with guidance for one more ruling and FIX round, or stop the flow.`

**One automatic round; any extra round asks the human.** If the PR is still held after the `FIX`, the flow waits for a human answer (nax entry), which starts exactly one more `RULE` + `FIX` round with the answer as guidance. The human can stop instead (the existing stop route).

**A red gate is the agent's to fix**: `FIX` tries the code fix; the guided `RULE` after it re-runs the gate and rules `fixed <sha>` when it is green.

**CI holds stop.** A `FIX` whose `readyHeld` starts with `CI ` stops `pr_not_ready` (nobody can rule a CI item). Thread-entry flows keep F4b's behaviour: no waits, a held `FIX` stops `pr_not_ready` and `RULE` questions stop `review_ambiguous`.

Add nax-entry FIX hold cases to flow-step-decision.spec.ts. The existing FIX cases keep canApplyCalls: false and their assertions are unchanged. This story only changes decisions; US-011 writes the wait and dispatches the guided task.

**Scope** — In: rules 6-9, exact hold question, answer-job matching and CI/thread stops. Out: RULE verdict decisions (US-007), payload widening (US-009), actual wait/outbox/guided dispatch wiring (US-011), answer API changes. Waits for thread-entry flows; they keep F4b's stop behaviour. Turning human answers directly into rulings; answers are guidance for a new RULE job.

**Interface** — Reuse US-007's widened FlowStepAction: `{ kind: 'wait_answer'; step: 'FIX'; jobId: string; questions: FlowQuestion[] }` or `{ kind: 'dispatch'; step: 'RULE'; rule: { answeredJobId: string | null } }`.

Answer with guidance for one more ruling and FIX round, or stop the flow.' }] }.
[unit] The same FIX with questionsJobId equal to its id and non-null answers returns { kind: 'dispatch', step: 'RULE', rule: { answeredJobId: <id> } }.

**Motivation** — Live flows 7-9 (fleet design doc §9.174-§9.176) reach `FIX`, but a draft PR whose open items need rulings stops the flow `pr_not_ready`, and the human has to rule each item through `POST .../fleet/jobs/:id/rulings` and dispatch `FIX` by hand.

**Approach** — `FleetFlowQuestionsPayload` and `parseFlowQuestionsPayload` (`apps/api/src/notifications/fleet/fleet-notification-events.ts:33`, :104). Target: `step` accepts `RULE` and `FIX`.

`formatQuestionsComment` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-calls.ts:79`). Target: `step` accepts `RULE` and `FIX`.

Widen `FleetFlowQuestionsPayload.step`, `parseFlowQuestionsPayload` and `formatQuestionsComment` to `RULE` and `FIX`. Add RULE/FIX accepted-step cases to fleet-notification-events.spec.ts; the existing malformed-step PLAN case is unchanged. Add the FIX questions-comment case to flow-calls.spec.ts; existing assertions are unchanged. Existing question-format tests also live in flow-questions.spec.ts. Keep F4b's existing outbox consumers: the ticket subscriber and notification subscriber both parse the payload, and the generic comment body starts `Flow needs answers (<step> job <id>):`. No new notification producer or consumer is necessary.

**Scope** — In: payload step union and runtime allowlist, unchanged validation of other fields, comment formatter step type and behavioral cases. Out: decisions (US-007/008), wait/outbox emission (US-011), database fan-out scenario (US-012), new answer routes and UI. A notification when a flow completes.

**Interface**
```ts
// FleetFlowQuestionsPayload.step and formatQuestionsComment input.step
```

userStories.title: Load PR ruling inputs and dispatch guided RULE rounds
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fill the optional PR-phase decision inputs, pass RUN-based RULE task data through dispatch, and reuse the existing FIX wait writer.

**Motivation** — Live flows 7-9 (fleet design doc §9.174-§9.176) reach `FIX`, but a draft PR whose open items need rulings stops the flow `pr_not_ready`, and the human has to rule each item through `POST .../fleet/jobs/:id/rulings` and dispatch `FIX` by hand.

**Approach** — `decisionInput` (only when the latest job's step is `REVIEW` or `RULE`): `run` from `latestJobForStep(flowId, 'RUN')`'s `workflow` (null when no RUN or no workflow), `ruledItemIds` from `FleetPrRulingsService.ruledItemIds(run.id)` (called only when that RUN has a non-null `workflow`; empty otherwise), `rulingsJobId` from the feature.

**Decision inputs load lazily.** `run` and `ruledItemIds` are read only when the latest job is `REVIEW` or `RULE`, so earlier steps add no reads.

`RULE` dispatch: `ref` = the RUN's `resultBranch`, `prNumber` = the feature PR, items = `ruleTaskItems(run.openItems, ruledItemIds)`, guidance = when `answeredJobId` is set, the feature's stored `questions` and `answers` plus `held` = that job's `fixReady.readyHeld` when it is a `FIX` (else null).

**RULE ref** is the RUN's `resultBranch` (the PR's head branch), so a guided round sees `FIX`'s push.

`DispatchPass` gains optional `rule?: { ref: string; prNumber: number; items: FlowOpenItem[]; guidance: FlowRuleGuidance | null }`, read inside the decide transaction like `plan` and passed to `buildStepDispatch` (US-011). A guided RULE after FIX must still load its RUN for dispatch data even though FIX does not trigger decisionInput's lazy REVIEW/RULE read. The RUN returned by the repository is a FleetJobRecord: read resultBranch from that record and openItems from its workflow.openItems; FlowStepInput.run is only the workflow projection, not the job record. A guided RULE always runs, irrespective of needsAutomaticRule. Missing RUN.resultBranch stops `dispatch_refused`, detail `RULE: RUN has no result branch`.

`FleetFlowAdvanceService` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/fleet-flow-advance.service.ts`). Target: `decisionInput` fills `run`, `ruledItemIds`, `rulingsJobId`; `RULE` dispatch reads the RUN, the guidance and the held reason; `writeDecision`'s `wait_answer` branch works unchanged for the new steps. A FIX wait uses setWaiting and the existing fleet_flow_questions outbox event, preserving its transactional audit/activity and per-job event id. US-009 widens the consumer contract; this story must not absorb that independent story or add a dependency.

The existing 'dispatches the exact FIX body' case in fleet-flow-advance.service.spec.ts has a COMPLETED REVIEW as its latest job and a latestJobForStep stub returning the PLAN job for any step; that PLAN job has no workflow, so ruledItemIds is not called and the FIX body assertion is unchanged. Add RULE-dispatch and FIX-wait cases to fleet-flow-advance-answers.spec.ts; existing assertions are unchanged (their latest jobs are SPEC_REVIEW/PRD_REVIEW, so the lazy RUN read is not triggered). FleetFlowsService.answer remains step-agnostic and unchanged.

**Scope** — In: lazy decision reads, RUN task items/protected ids, current-branch RULE ref, answered-job guidance, missing-branch stop, dispatch seam and existing wait/outbox path. Out: action selection (US-007/008), question payload widening (US-009), ruling batch recording (US-010), real-DB scenario (US-012). Refreshing a RUN's stored `openItems` after a FIX; rulings stay bound to the RUN snapshot (Arc A). Turning human answers directly into rulings; answers are guidance for a new RULE job.

**Interface**
```ts
rule?: { ref: string; prNumber: number; items: FlowOpenItem[]; guidance: FlowRuleGuidance | null };
// FlowRuleGuidance
{ held: string | null; questions: FlowQuestion[]; answers: FlowAnswer[] };
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With a COMPLETED REVIEW as the latest job, decisionInput passes run from the latest RUN's workflow, ruledItemIds from FleetPrRulingsService.ruledItemIds(runId) and rulingsJobId from the feature to decideFlowStep.

userStories.title: Exercise PR-phase ruling and guided rounds against PostgreSQL
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the binding integration scenario proving real flow/ruling/ticket/outbox persistence from draft RUN through a guided RULE round.

**Motivation** — Live flows 7-9 (fleet design doc §9.174-§9.176) reach `FIX`, but a draft PR whose open items need rulings stops the flow `pr_not_ready`, and the human has to rule each item through `POST .../fleet/jobs/:id/rulings` and dispatch `FIX` by hand.

**Approach** — An integration spec driving a nax-entry flow from a draft RUN through RULE, recorded rulings, FIX dispatch with the rulings snapshot, a held FIX, the wait, the answers and the guided RULE.

Create apps/api/test/integration/fleet/fleet-flow-rulings.integration.spec.ts. Use fleet-flow-answers.integration.spec.ts for NAX-entry seeding, answer execution and explicit FanOutPublisher publication; fleet-flow-advance.integration.spec.ts for advancing linked terminal jobs; and fleet-pr-rulings-ingest.integration.spec.ts for real ruling/FIX/ticket persistence patterns. Explicitly seed workflow.outcome='draft', workflow.openItems (D-1 advisor, F-1 finding), RUN.resultBranch, canonical PR URL, completed REVIEW and strictly ordered job times. The ingest fixture is only a seeding precedent; do not assume it already has workflow.openItems. Stub the item-index forge read to find the marker and the PR head read for the FIX snapshot; do not mock away the writer, repositories, advance decisions, question consumers or PostgreSQL.

The single FIX that follows carries those rulings (`--rulings`), fixes the findings, and readies the PR. That is the one automatic round. When FIX leaves the PR held (a red gate, items it could not close), a nax-entry flow asks the human instead of stopping: one ticket comment and notification (the F4b question path), and the human's answer is the guidance for one more RULE + FIX round. Every further round needs a new answer. CI holds still stop.

Publish the fleet_flow_questions event through the real F4b fan-out to observe the question comment and notification; it is distinct from the RUN Finish ticket's RULING comment. Disable background relay/sweeps for deterministic assertions, use real creator/approver fixtures and restore forge stubs. Use canRunDbTests() and run bun run test:scoped test/integration/fleet/fleet-flow-rulings.integration.spec.ts outside NAX_SANDBOXED=1 with KODA_DB_TESTS=1 enabled by the scoped command. Database skips do not verify this story. Do not run database-resetting suites concurrently against the same test database.

**Scope** — In: the explicitly declared integration-test story and its PR-phase seam behaviors, including SYSTEM comment authors, snapshot attribution, waiting/answers, the F4b question notification and CI stopping. Out: production logic already delivered by US-001 through US-011, answer API/DTO changes, new frontend/CLI behavior. A web form for answering or showing rulings (F6); the flow DTO is unchanged. A notification when a flow completes.

**Interface** — Drive the existing `FleetFlowAdvanceService.advance(flowId: string, now: Date): Promise<void>` or its FleetFlowTicker wrapper, `FleetFlowsService.answer`, and the existing FanOutPublisher; do not add a test-only production route.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] A nax-entry flow whose RUN is a draft with open items D-1 (advisor) and F-1 (finding), after a COMPLETED REVIEW, dispatches a RULE AGENT job on the next advance tick.

[integration] With that RULE job COMPLETED and output ending {"rulings":[{"item":"D-1","ruling":"verified: test green"}],"questions":[]}, the next tick stores one FleetPrRuling for D-1 with actorType SYSTEM, actorId flow and state pending, and sets the feature's rulingsJobId to the RULE job id (the item-index forge read stubbed to find the marker).
[integration] The RUN's Finish ticket carries a RULING comment 'D-1 (advisor): verified: test green (flow <flowId>)' with no author user or agent.
[integration] The following tick dispatches a FIX job whose prRulings snapshot (PR head read stubbed) contains the D-1 ruling with by: 'koda:system:flow'.

[integration] With that FIX COMPLETED and fixReady: { markedReady: false, readyHeld: '1 open item(s): G-1' }, the next tick moves the flow and feature to WAITING_ANSWER with questionsJobId equal to the FIX id, and, after publishing that tick's questions outbox event through FanOutPublisher, the questions ticket comment starts 'Flow needs answers (FIX job <id>):'.

Goal and done: extend the existing single-feature PR phase from RUN -> REVIEW -> FIX to RUN -> REVIEW -> conditional RULE -> FIX. RULE is a read-only reviewer-model AGENT job that returns evidenced Arc A rulings, never a code-writing replacement for FIX. There is one automatic round. A non-CI held FIX in a NAX-entry flow waits for one human answer, which authorizes exactly one further guided RULE + FIX round; further holds need fresh answers. CI holds and THREAD-entry holds still stop. Done includes durable SYSTEM/flow rulings, their FIX snapshot, replay safety, refusal reporting, guidance and question fan-out, and a PostgreSQL-backed end-to-end PR-phase scenario.
